newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-ITALIAN COACHES FIGHT FOR GERMAN SUPREMACY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN COACHES FIGHT FOR GERMAN SUPREMACY.

text.p: Italians Giovanni Trapattoni and Nevio Scala promise to be among the most important figures in German soccer this season.
Bayern Munich coach Trapattoni won his first duel with his Borussia Dortmund counterpart Scala when the German champions beat their main rivals 2-0 in a German League Cup semifinal on Wednesday.

"It was a good test but nothing more," said Scala, who joined the European Cup winners from Italian side Perugia. He said the serious business really starts on August 3 when Dortmund play promoted Herta Berlin in their first Bundesliga game.
Scala became the second Italian coach in the German league last month after Ottmar Hitzfeld decided to quit and take over a new position as club sports director.
An opera lover who has a German wife and speaks fluent German, Scala led Parma from the Italian second division to the European elite with triumphs in the 1993 Cup Winners' Cup and the 1995 UEFA Cup.
But his achievements look pale compared to Trapattoni's.
"Scala speaks better German but Trapattoni has had more success," said Dortmund international defender Juergen Kohler, who knows them both.

Trapattoni, who joined Bayern at the start of last season after a previous stint in 1994-95, had established himself as the most successful coach in Italy by leading both Juventus and Internazionale to a total eight titles.
His life at Bayern was not an easy one last season as the club's winning campaign was marred by squabbling and scandals.
Striker Juergen Klinsmann, who eventually left for Sampdoria, once yelled at Trapattoni for being substituted and Bayern was nicknamed Hollywood City for its constant drama.
The atmosphere at Dortmund is not quite as turbulent. In a way, the flamboyant Trapattoni and the quiet Scala have each chosen a club suited to their temperaments.
They used to play together at AC Milan in the late 1960s, winning the Cup Winners' Cup final against Hamburg in 1968.
"He was an elegant technician, I was a useful, strong player," recalled Scala.
The two face heavy responsibilities this season as both Bayern and Borussia aim to win the German title and European Cup.

Bayern will rely on a revamped team with new foreign signings such as Brazilian striker Giovane Elber, who joined from Stuttgart for 12.5 million marks ($6.94 million) and French international defender Bixente Lizarazu.
Dortmund will rely on a squad similar to the one which beat Juventus in the European Cup final last May with strong individual players such as Kohler and playmaker Andreas Moeller.
"We're not ready yet but I liked what I saw tonight," said Trapattoni after the victory over Dortmund.
"We've still got time," said Scala. "I'm not worried because there is plenty of talent in the team."
